Claire — thanks for the clear pull-out. Appreciate the context.

We reviewed your redlines and have attached a consolidated counter (QH_consolidated_redline.docx) that flags where Redwood can accept narrow carve-outs and where we need alternative language. Summary of our positions below: 

1) Output ownership / assignment
- We cannot accept a broad assignment of output that assigns title to all generated outputs. That would conflict with standard model IP allocations and our obligations to other customers.
- We can agree to a narrowly scoped, time-limited assignment for outputs that are a direct, one-to-one transformation of QuantaHealth proprietary input data and that are incorporated into a named product feature on QuantaHealth's platform. Proposed language: a nonexclusive, perpetual (for the specific feature), royalty-free assignment limited to the specific outputs identified by exhibit and produced during the initial 12-month pilot window. This addresses their need for productization while protecting Redwood's broader model outputs.

2) Training / Model Use opt-out
- We can accept an explicit opt-out for use of QuantaHealth-provided data and outputs for model training or improvement. We will classify that data with a tenant-level tag and exclude it from training pipelines.
- We cannot provide guarantees that are technically infeasible (for example, irrevocable deletion from third-party open-source snapshots). The opt-out applies to Redwood-controlled training and improvements, documented in an annex.

3) Telemetry / auditing
- We can retain telemetry/usage tags for 18 months as requested, with exportable audit reports upon reasonable request and under NDAs where appropriate. We will not surface raw token streams externally but can provide aggregated and per-request metadata.

4) Feedback license
- We propose a narrow feedback license: QuantaHealth grants Redwood a limited, nonexclusive right to use anonymized feedback to improve service quality (metrics and bug fixes), subject to the training opt-out above. If QuantaHealth wishes to opt completely out of any feedback use, we need to discuss commercial offsets.

Attachments: QH_consolidated_redline.docx (tracked consolidations)

If these tradeoffs look reasonable we can circulate the consolidated redline to procurement and prepare a DocuSign-ready Order Form. Diego — can you confirm product/engineering feasibility for the tenant-level tagging and training exclusion? Ben — please advise on pricing offset options for a full feedback opt-out vs. partial license.

Claire — happy to jump on a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk language and exhibits.

Best — Laura
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Diego — thanks for the fast turnaround and the consolidated redline. I reviewed the proposed carve-outs with our product and legal teams; overall the compromise looks workable. A couple of clarifying notes before we finalize:

- Exhibit approach: QuantaHealth will provide an exhibit listing the proprietary input datasets and named features that should fall within the narrow assignment. We'll expect Redwood's consolidated redline to reference that exhibit by ID.
- Audit exports: the audit reports you referenced — can those be delivered on a monthly cadence during the initial 12-month pilot? If so, procurement is comfortable with 18 months retention.
